slides.title: Rows are / the [unit]
slides.text: A table answers by row: one entity, its values, and the column names that say what each value means.

steps: Find the table and its title: the caption, or the heading above it.
Keep the header rows apart from the body rows.
Pack whole rows up to the size limit, with rows for the same key (Frankfurt) together.
Put the title and header on top of every chunk.
A row too wide for the limit: split by columns and repeat the key column.

slides.title: One-line HTML / cuts [mid-row]
slides.text: The same table as HTML on one line has no `\n` and no spaces between cells, so the splitter cuts at 300 characters:
bullets: Virginia's cold-tier egress price, `0.09`, starts the next chunk, away from its region.
Chunk 1 ends inside the caption, at `per GB,`.
Parse HTML tables into rows before you chunk them.

slides.title: Repeat the / [header]
slides.text: Group whole rows by region and put the title and header on top. Chunk 3 of 6 at 300 characters:
slides.after: Each chunk now names its table and its columns, and all three Frankfurt tiers come back together.

slides.title: Whole rows, / grouped by [key]
slides.text: The chunker behind that slide (rows sorted by key):

visuals.code:
md = lambda c: "| " + " | ".join(c) + " |"

def chunk_table(title, header, rows,
                key=0, max_chars=300):
    top = [title, md(header),
           "|---" * len(header) + "|"]
    out, cur = [], []
    for _, g in {{groupby(rows, lambda r: r[key])}}:
        g = [md(r) for r in g]
        size = len("\n".join(top + cur + g))
        if cur and size > max_chars:
            out.append(top + cur); cur = []
        cur += g
    return ["\n".join(c) for c in out + [top + cur]]

bullets: Title and header: 102 characters, about a third of the 300-character limit.
A key whose rows pass `max_chars` stays one chunk; split it by rows.

slides.title: Docling repeats / the [header]
slides.text: Docling's `HybridChunker` (docling-core 2.107.1) with `MarkdownTableSerializer` and a word-count tokenizer at `max_tokens=100`:

visuals.label: Chunk 2 of 3 (first rows, padding trimmed)
visuals.code:
{{| Region | Tier | Storage | Egress | Days |}}
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frankfurt | Cool | 0.014 | 0.10 | 30 |
| Frankfurt | Cold | 0.005 | 0.12 | 90 |

bullets: `repeat_table_header=True` is the default. The caption stays in chunk 1 only, so add the title to each chunk yourself.
Rows aren't grouped by key: Frankfurt Hot ended chunk 1, its other tiers opened chunk 2.

slides.title: Across rows, / use [SQL]
slides.text: "Which region has the cheapest egress for the Cold tier?" needs all 6 Cold rows. The row groups put one in each of 6 chunks.

For totals, rankings and filters, load the table into a database and have the model write SQL (Text-to-SQL).

cards.title: Use it when
items: Questions look up one entity's values: a region, a plan, a SKU
Your parser keeps the header row and the caption
A key's rows fit your chunk size with the header on top

cards.title: Move on when
items: Questions total, rank or filter across rows: Text-to-SQL
Cells hold paragraphs: chunk each row as text with its column names
Rows wider than the limit: split columns, repeat the key

slides.title: [Cheat] sheet
rows: Chunk whole rows; cut between rows
Title and header rows on top of every chunk
Keep rows for the same key in one chunk
One-line HTML tables: parse into rows first
Docling repeats the header row; add the caption yourself (2.107.1)
Over-wide rows: split columns, repeat the key column
Totals and rankings across rows: Text-to-SQL

slides.line: Legal text has its own unit too: the numbered clause, with its section number in every chunk.
